messages:
Sam: Heads-up — after yesterday's kernel selector change we see a ~18% drop in prefix cache hit rate for short-chat workload. CPU/GPU profiles attached in the thread.
Anya: Oof. Same 770B model? any change to key derivation or batching?
Sam: Yep same model. The change picked a different fused-attn kernel for seq_len 128 which reduced per-token latency slightly, but profiling shows more KV cache churn + more cache-key collisions.
Michael: Do we have an example request that misses but should hit?
Sam: Pasting a minimal example of headers we get from the SDK when streaming + retry:
```
POST /v1/generate
Host: api.redwood.ai
Authorization: Bearer xxxxx
X-RW-Prefetch: 1
X-RW-Cache-Opt: true
X-Request-Id: r-123
TE: trailers
Connection: keep-alive
```
Anya: The kernel change reordered some internal KV map hashing (changed salt when switching from cuda_kernel_v2 -> cuda_kernel_v3). That explains collisions if cache key included kernel-specific salt.
Kate: Wait, cache keys include the runtime fingerprint? I thought keys were only prompt+model+user-provided-id.
Sam: They should be, but a bug in the selector introduced `runtime_salt` into the canonicalization path for warmstart keys. It only shows up when the SDK sets `X-RW-Prefetch: 1` and the request is served from streaming prefetch path.
Michael: Ah. So kernel selection is leaking into stable key material — that will make warm starts fragile across minor runtime changes.
Anya: Quick mitigation: normalize the keying path to strip runtime-specific salts before hashing. Also add asserting unit tests to catch salt changes.
Sam: Agreed. Also noticed retries are causing duplicate attempts without copying the cache headers. The retry flow omits `X-RW-Cache-Opt` sometimes, so second attempt misses even if first would populate.
Kate: That's a streaming edge-case: the chunked retry path spins up a new connection and doesn't copy some optional headers. We should make SDK always preserve cache opt-ins across retries.
perf-bot: perf/regression detected: prefix_cache_hit_rate short-chat 0.82 -> 0.67 after deploy (p < 0.001).
Michael: Proposed short plan:
- patch runtime to remove `runtime_salt` from cache key canonicalization (hotfix)
- add SDK change to persist cache opt headers across retries and streaming reconnects
- add a warmstart prefetch job in Dedicated to pre-warm popular prefixes on kernel rollouts
- add unit + integration tests for canonical keys across kernels
Sam: I ran a local microbenchmark. With canonicalization fix applied, simulated workload hit-rate goes back to 0.84 and end-to-end p50 improves ~7%. Raw numbers:
```
before: hit_rate=0.67, p50=74ms, p95=210ms
after:  hit_rate=0.84, p50=69ms, p95=198ms
```
Anya: Nice. For the warmstart strategy, can we prefetch top-500 prefixes per model during kernel rollout window (respecting opt-in headers)? Prefer a job that keys off usage telemetry.
Kate: Need to watch budgets — prefetching increases token-cost during rollout. Maybe progressive warmstart: stage 1 = top 100, stage 2 = 100-500 if hit-rate improves.
Michael: Also a rollout policy: pin kernel selector for existing KV entries for 24h. So in case of kernel churn, we avoid rekeying active cache entries.
Sam: That's clever — keep KV lookup to the selector used when the entry was created (store selector id in metadata) until TTL expires.
Anya: Implementation note: don't encode selector id into the raw cache hash; keep it in metadata and use it as a fallback. Cleaner than changing global canonicalization.
Kate: SDK changes needed: 1) ensure `X-RW-Cache-Opt` is always sent when user opted in; 2) add `x-rw-cache-client-id` so we can tie retries/streams to same logical op; 3) `prefer-stable-key: true` header for rollout windows.
Sam: I'll open runtime PR for the canonicalization hotfix and metadata fallback. Anya can own the SDK PR for header persistence + client-id. Michael — can you run the warmstart budget simulation?
Michael: On it. I'll simulate traffic and budget impact and post numbers. Expected to be acceptable if we stage.
perf-bot: task created: PERF-3412 (investigate prefix caching regression)
Kate: Thanks — if we can get the hotfix out in the next deploy window that should reduce user impact. :thumbsup:
Sam: I'll attach the PRs and followups here. For traceability, keep all rollback/experiment flags visible in console.
Anya: Also adding an invariant test that canonical key output is identical across kernel versions for same input. That should catch future regressions.
Sam: Great. Closing loop — will update when PRs land.
Kate: lgtm
Michael: thanks everyone
